Chapter 5
from one channel. A high image-text similarity, an OCR confidence, and
a language-model token probability refer to different events and sample
spaces. Multiplying them assumes a probabilistic model and dependence
structure that usually has not been established. A decision-level calibrator
can instead be trained and assessed against verified target selection or task
outcomes, with separate evaluation under appearance and temporal shifts.
Calibration then supports an explicit refresh or abstention policy rather
than decorating an uncertain action with an unjustified numerical score.
83

Agentic State
Chapter 16
MATM’s state keys address procedural matching, and MemCalib addresses
use after evidence is supplied. Combining them is a design hypothesis, not
an established composite result.
The original synthesis is to view retrieval as a controlled transition from
stored evidence to active decision state. The transition must preserve
source identity, role, time, and access scope as well as content. Its success
is measured by justified behavior under bounded cost, not by the number
of records returned. Chapter 17 places this transition within a unified
consistency model linking the stored history, assembled context, policy,
tools, and environment.
241

Agentic State
Chapter 17
state which transitions are exact, which are approximate, which depend on
model judgment, and which are unknown.
The cross-layer conclusion is that context, memory, and policy must
evolve under compatible contracts. More storage does not repair wrong
conditioning; correct transactions do not make a false abstraction true; a
current model does not make old skills compatible; and a well-formed tool
call does not establish authorization. Treating these distinctions together
provides a technical basis for reliable stateful execution without claiming a
general solution to intelligence.
